For a first-order reaction, how many half-lives are required for 75% completion?

text_solutions:
For a first-order reaction, after \( n \) half-lives, \( [\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 \left( \frac{1}{2} \right)^n \).

75% completion means 25% remains, so \( \frac{[\text{R}]}{[\text{R}]_0} = 0.25 = \left( \frac{1}{2} \right)^2 \).

Thus, \( n = 2 \) half-lives.

A reaction has a rate constant with units \( \text{mol}^{-1} \text{L} \text{s}^{-1} \). What is the order of the reaction?

text_solutions:
For a reaction of order \( n \), the unit of \( k \) is \( (\text{mol L}^{-1})^{1-n} \text{s}^{-1} \).

Given unit: \( \text{mol}^{-1} \text{L} \text{s}^{-1} = (\text{mol L}^{-1})^{-1} \text{s}^{-1} \).

\( 1 - n = -1 \), \( n = 2 \). Thus, the order is 2.

New rate = \( k \left( \frac{[\text{A}]}{2} \right) (3[\text{B}])^2 = k \times \frac{[\text{A}]}{2} \times 9 [\text{B}]^2 = \frac{9}{2} k [\text{A}] [\text{B}]^2 \).
